brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.evidence: Drawer drawer:0#0,1#cut sits on the cut face of half-n base piece:0,1,0 (socket s2, slot 's'). Spike spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 stands at the three-cell junction of (0,0),(0,1),(1,0). Build has 1 drawer and 1 spike.

requirements.requirement: Both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching
requirements.evidence: Both features are on the same cell (0,1): the drawer is on its cut face and the spike's junction includes (0,1). The tools only offer the drawer by cell and face slot, and the spike by junction, so I could not confirm from the data that the drawer's footprint is at the same corner vertex as the spike. The spike was offered only at this junction, and the drawer only at this slot, so that is the closest match the configurator allows. check_build: rule errors none; meshClash clear. Warnings: LOOSE_BODY between half-n and full base (joint bolts would lock them, not requested).

finish.summary: Built three bases (full at 0,0 and 1,0; north half at 0,1), added a drawer on the half-n cut face and a spike at the junction of cells (0,0),(0,1),(1,0). The mesh check is clear. The corner match is the weak point: the tools don't report the drawer's corner vertex, so I can only confirm both features share cell (0,1) and the spike's junction.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
